reports.title: Strait of Malacca — strategic chokepoint and transit statistics/context
reports.publisher: Derived from international maritime/energy analyses + Indonesian sovereignty context (Sumatra side)
reports.description: The primary western gateway between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea / Pacific. Handles a very large share of global maritime trade and an even larger share of seaborne energy flows from the Middle East and Africa to East Asia. Indonesia controls a significant portion of the southern coastline. Continuously cited in energy-security, shipping and geopolitical analysis.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality maritime-chokepoint node for Indonesia. Critical for understanding why the archipelago sits at the centre of Asian energy security.

reports.title: Sunda Strait — alternative passage statistics/context
reports.publisher: Derived from maritime and Indonesian official context
reports.description: Major alternative route between the Indian Ocean and the Java Sea / internal Indonesian waters. Shallower and more constrained than Lombok; used as a partial substitute when Malacca is stressed. Fully under Indonesian sovereignty.
reports._notes: Key alternative-passage node under full Indonesian control.

reports.title: Lombok and Makassar Straits — deep-water alternative passages
reports.publisher: Derived from maritime analyses + Indonesian sovereignty
reports.description: Deep-water alternative routes preferred by the largest deep-draft tankers and bulk carriers (especially when Malacca draft is limiting) and by traffic linked to Australia. Also strategically relevant for submarine transit. Entirely within Indonesian archipelagic waters.
reports._notes: Deep-water redundancy nodes that raise Indonesia’s strategic maritime centrality.
_referenced_by: Australian and East Asian trade-route studies

reports.title: Indonesian Archipelagic Sea Lanes (ALKI) and archipelagic-state regime
reports.publisher: Government of Indonesia / UNCLOS-related practice
reports.description: The formal Archipelagic Sea Lanes (ALKI) designated under the archipelagic-state regime of UNCLOS. Legal and operational frame that governs transit through Indonesian waters while preserving sovereignty. Recurring citation in maritime policy, defence and international-law contexts.
reports._notes: Foundational legal-regime node for all Indonesian chokepoint and transit analysis.
_referenced_by: Malacca, Sunda, Lombok and Makassar nodes

reports.title: Inter-island connectivity and logistics policy/statistics
reports.publisher: Derived from BPS transport statistics, Ministry of Transportation, and connectivity programmes
reports.description: Statistical and policy traces of inter-island shipping, port connectivity and logistics programmes intended to reduce price disparities and integrate the domestic market across the archipelago.
reports._notes: Domestic-integration counterpart to the international chokepoint nodes.

reports.title: Indonesia maritime-chokepoint, inter-provincial trade and special-zone meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from maritime, BPS trade, SEZ/FTZ and customs sources
reports.description: Meta-node that binds the Strait of Malacca, Sunda Strait, Lombok–Makassar passages, Archipelagic Sea Lanes regime, inter-provincial and inter-island trade statistics, Special Economic Zones, Free Trade/Free Port Zones, customs/tariff regime, and inter-island connectivity policy into a single high-centrality cluster. Captures both Indonesia’s role as a global energy and trade transit state and its internal commercial diversity across thousands of islands.
reports._notes: High-mass integrating node for the strategic-geography and internal-diversity layer requested by the user.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Energy, trade, provincial and external-sector series from earlier batches

reports.description: Meta-node binding defence budget and archipelagic posture, education statistics and tertiary GER, construction sector statistics, paddy/rice production, sea and multimodal transport, gender statistics, and provincial CPI into a coherent multi-domain densification layer.
reports._notes: Integrating node for the multi-domain research rounds in Batch 11.

reports.title: Geographic distribution of religious communities
reports.publisher: Derived from census and civil-registration data
reports.description: Spatial patterning of religious affiliation — Muslim majority almost everywhere, with notable Hindu concentration in Bali, Christian majorities or large minorities in parts of eastern Indonesia (North Sulawesi, Papua, Maluku, NTT, etc.), and other local patterns.
reports._notes: Spatial densification of the religion cluster; links identity to the archipelagic geography already mapped.
_referenced_by: Provincial and Bali–Nusa Tenggara / Papua / Sulawesi nodes

reports._notes: High-density bilateral relationship node sitting on the Malacca approaches.

reports.title: Java water-stress and water-security framing
reports.publisher: Derived from water-supply, agricultural and planning sources
reports.description: Recurring policy and analytical framing of water stress on Java — high population density, intensive agriculture, industrial demand and seasonal variability. Complements the national water-supply statistics with a spatially focused narrative.
reports._notes: Spatial water-stress node that tightens the Java environmental and infrastructure cluster.
_referenced_by: Water Supply Statistics and irrigation indicators

reports.title: Java economic and demographic core
reports.publisher: Derived from BPS provincial and national statistics
reports.region: Java (DKI Jakarta, West Java, Central Java, DIY, East Java, Banten)
reports.description: Relational node capturing Java’s dominant share of population, GDP, manufacturing and services. Forms the primary core against which outer-island resource economies are contrasted.
reports._notes: High-level spatial core node for the archipelago.

reports.title: Outer-islands resource and demographic periphery
reports.publisher: Derived from BPS provincial statistics
reports.region: Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Maluku, Papua, Nusa Tenggara, etc.
reports.description: Relational node for the non-Java provinces that collectively hold the majority of land area and resource wealth (palm oil, coal, nickel, gas, etc.) but a minority of population and manufacturing. Captures the classic core–periphery structure of the Indonesian economy.
reports._notes: Periphery counterpart to the Java core. Essential for later densification of specific resource provinces.

reports.title: Downstreaming / hilirisasi industrial-policy statistics and framing
reports.publisher: Derived from Ministry of Industry / ESDM / BPS trade and production data; recurring in official policy
reports.description: Statistical and policy traces of the downstreaming (hilirisasi) strategy that bans or restricts raw mineral exports and promotes domestic processing (especially nickel). Continuously cited in industrial and trade policy.
reports._notes: High-citation industrial-policy node unique to contemporary Indonesia.
_referenced_by: Foreign-trade composition (shift from ore to intermediates)

reports.title: Indonesia commodity and spatial-resource meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from BPS, ESDM and related sources
reports.description: Meta-node that binds palm oil, nickel, coal, broader mining, PDRB, Java-core vs outer-islands contrast, and the hilirisasi policy frame into a coherent resource-and-space cluster. Captures the dual structure of a Java-centred industrial/service economy and an outer-island resource economy.
reports._notes: Integrating node for the resource–spatial uniqueness of Indonesia.
_referenced_by: All commodity and provincial nodes in this batch
National accounts, trade and energy series

reports.title: Sumatra regional statistical profile
reports.publisher: BPS provincial offices / national BPS
reports.description: Aggregate and key provincial statistics for the Sumatra island group — major palm-oil, coal, oil & gas and plantation economy; significant population and land area.
reports._notes: Primary western outer-island resource region.

reports.title: Kalimantan regional statistical profile
reports.publisher: BPS provincial offices / national BPS
reports.description: Statistics for the Kalimantan provinces — dominant coal, palm-oil, forestry and emerging industrial roles; large land area and low population density relative to Java.
reports._notes: Core Borneo resource region; also site of the new capital project context.
_referenced_by: New capital (IKN) related planning where relevant

reports.title: Sulawesi regional statistical profile (nickel focus)
reports.publisher: BPS provincial offices / national BPS
reports.description: Statistics for Sulawesi provinces — central to the nickel mining and downstream processing boom, with significant agricultural and fisheries activity.
reports._notes: Geographic anchor of the nickel downstreaming story.

reports.title: Papua regional statistical profile (including new provinces)
reports.publisher: BPS provincial offices / national BPS
reports.description: Statistics for the Papua provinces — vast land area, low population density, resource potential (minerals, forest), distinctive demographic and development indicators, and recent administrative splitting into multiple provinces.
reports._notes: Easternmost and most distinctive regional node; administrative structure still evolving.
_referenced_by: Provincial population, poverty and PDRB series

reports.title: Bali and Nusa Tenggara tourism-oriented regional profile
reports.publisher: BPS provincial offices / national BPS
reports.description: Statistics for Bali and the Nusa Tenggara provinces — tourism-heavy (especially Bali), distinctive cultural and demographic profiles, and different development challenges from the large resource islands.
reports._notes: Tourism-specialised regional contrast to the resource outer islands.
